items.stem: Users search both for exact error codes and for paraphrased questions. What retrieval design fits best?

options.text: Hybrid search combining keyword (for exact terms) and vector (for paraphrases)
options.rationale: Correct: hybrid covers both exact-match and semantic queries.
Pure vector search can miss exact identifiers like error codes.
Pure keyword search handles paraphrases poorly.

items.explanation: Correct: hybrid covers both exact-match and semantic queries.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices make combining two retrievers sound? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use a rank-fusion method such as reciprocal rank fusion
options.rationale: Correct: RRF combines rankings without needing comparable raw scores.

options.text: Normalise scores before weighting if you combine raw scores
options.rationale: Correct: normalisation makes scores from different retrievers comparable.

options.text: Add raw scores from both retrievers directly
options.rationale: Unnormalised scores are not comparable and distort the mix.

options.text: Use only the first retriever's results and discard the other
options.rationale: Discarding a signal defeats the purpose of hybrid search.

items.explanation: Correct: RRF combines rankings without needing comparable raw scores.

items.stem: A cross-encoder reranker improves relevance but you must rerank quickly. What is the usual approach?

options.text: Rerank only a small candidate set from the first-stage retrievers
options.rationale: Correct: reranking a bounded candidate set controls latency while improving ordering.

options.text: Rerank the entire corpus on every query
options.rationale: Reranking everything is far too slow.
First-stage retrieval is what makes reranking tractable.

options.text: Rerank with a keyword matcher instead of the cross-encoder
options.rationale: That abandons the quality gain the cross-encoder provides.

items.explanation: Correct: reranking a bounded candidate set controls latency while improving ordering.
